entries.name: small-tuple-output-tuple_expr_one_item-v0#0
entries.description: sigmaProp(Tuple(1)._1 == 1) — a one-item tuple EXPRESSION. `TupleSerializer` writes a count and no type, so this round-trips verbatim; `Tuple.eval` then refuses it. The tree is the transaction's OUTPUT, at tree version 0 UNSIZED; the input is a plain `sigmaProp(true)` box and the output carries its whole value, so the Erg balance cannot mask anything. THE SEPARATING ROW of this pair: the JVM accepts the transaction, and an implementation whose tuples hold 2..255 refuses the output tree at parse with no size bit to degrade behind, so it rejects a VALID transaction.

entries.name: small-tuple-output-register_nested_tuple_expr#28
entries.description: R4 of the transaction's OUTPUT holds `Tuple(Tuple(1), 1)` — a pair whose FIRST item is a one-item tuple, as an EXPRESSION, under a plain `sigmaProp(true)` script. `TupleSerializer` writes a count and no type, so the JVM writes the register itself and the transaction is VALID. SEPARATING: an implementation whose tuples hold 2..255 refuses the nested one and rejects a valid transaction. There is deliberately no spend row — `((Int),Int)` is the only declared type `getReg` accepts and `TypeSerializer` cannot write it, so no script the JVM can write reads this register. It is valid, permanent and unreadable.
